messages.content: What is the dominant genetic trait of a Lion?

message.content: In lions, one of the most noticeable dominant traits is the presence of a mane in adult males. The gene that controls mane development is inherited in a dominant fashion—males that carry the dominant allele will develop a mane, while females (who are typically heterozygous) do not show the trait. This dominant allele is responsible for the characteristic dark, shaggy fur that surrounds the head and neck of male lions.
